sources.citation: Good, Jeff, Jesse Lovegren, Jean Patrick Mve, Carine Nganguep Tchiemouo, Rebecca Voll & Pierpaolo Di Carlo. 2011. The languages of the Lower Fungom region of Cameroon: Grammatical overview. Africana Linguistica 17: 101-164.
sources.note: Grammatical/phonological overview of the Yemne-Kimbi languages incl. Koshin (Bukwen's closest relative per Blench 2025/Glottolog); no Bukwen data, but the nearest proxy for prosodic typology of the Koshin-Bukwen node.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page bukw1238 (classification Yemne-Kimbi > Koshin-Bukwen; refs: Blench 2025 [listed as 'Blench 2005', 9 pp., comparative;wordlist] and Ethnologue 2025 only; 0 grammar/phonology/sketch refs).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; confirms no descriptive source exists.

sources.citation: Hamm, Cameron, Jason Diller, Kari Jordan-Diller & Ferdinand Assako a Tiati. 2002. A rapid appraisal survey of Western Beboid languages (Menchum Division, Northwest Province). ALCAM [876, 877, 878, 879]. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-014. Dallas: SIL International. 40 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives record 9061; academia.edu 36063557.)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing for Bukwen, and no phonology for any variety: it is a rapid-appraisal survey (lexicostatistics, reported intelligibility, vitality, names, demographics) of the Cameroonian Western Beboid villages Abar, Missong, Munken, Ngun, Fang, Koshin, Bu, Mundabli, Mufu, Mbu', Mashi (village), Mekaf. The only 'accent'/'tone' token in the whole text is questionnaire wording in the appendix ('Slight differences in accent/tone/etc.'). Bukwen appears once, by name only, as an unvisited Nigerian relative reported by Blench (p.c. 2000).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2025. The classification of the Bukwen language [buz] spoken in Mairogo, SE Nigeria. Circulation draft. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 9 pp. (Glottolog ref 700825; listed by Glottolog as a comparative study;wordlist). Full 9-page text is embedded in the academia.edu page (id 128924135), archived copy (Internet Archive) and extracted to txt.
sources.note: Nothing. Sections are Introduction, 'The controversial question of West Beboid', Analysis, Appendix (Table 1: c. 79-item Bukwen wordlist retyped from Koops 1971, tone-marked, with Mashi and external cognates; Table 2: Bu/Koshin/Mundabli). Tokens stress/accent/tone = 0/0/0. States 'The Bukwen language is known only from a short wordlist, collected by Robert Koops in Mairogo, SE Nigeria, in 1971.'

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Bukwen language' (cites Blench 2025 academia.edu and Blench 2011): 'The only data on Bukwen is found in a 1971 survey report by Robert Koops'.
Blench, Roger. 2024. An overview of the Bantoid languages. Afrika und Übersee 97: 1-46. doi:10.15460/auue.2024.97.1.288
sources.note: No mention of Bukwen; tone table rows only for Noone, Mundabli, etc.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. Cambridge: Mallam Dendo [Kay Williamson Educational Foundation]. 198 pp. (Glottolog reference 672362, listed by Glottolog as an overview; language code includes Bukwen [buz]; 2019 '4th edition' cited by en.wikipedia 'Beboid languages'.) Formerly downloadable at rogerblench.info/Language/Africa/Nigeria/Atlas of Nigerian Languages; archived copy (Internet Archive, 12 Jan 2026) exists.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing. The whole Bukwen entry is four lines (name, location 'Taraba State, near Takum', classification 'Benue-Congo: South Bantoid: Beboid', sources Koops 1971 and Blench 1992); no population, no dialects, no Refs. block, no phonology. a full-text search for stress/accent the 198-page PDF for tone/tonal/stress finds only front-matter remarks on tone-marking of reference names and bibliography titles for other languages; nothing on Bukwen prosody.

sources.citation: Ousmanou. 2014. How to Disclose the Environment through Linguistic Description: A Basic Linguistic Analysis of Koshin. PhD, Université de Yaoundé I. (closest relative of Bukwen per Blench 2025 / Glottolog Koshin-Bukwen node)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accently: no mention of Bukwen anywhere; describes Koshin, not Bukwen (not used as a statement for bukw1238).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2011. The membership and internal structure of Bantoid and the border with Bantu. Bantu IV, Humboldt University, Berlin (slides).
sources.note: No mention of Bukwen at all (a full-text search for stress/accent); Koops mss. mentioned only for Buru.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2009 draft. The Bantoid languages: a monograph (draft not for circulation). Sec. 5.5 Beboid (5.5.2 Classification, 5.5.3 Phonology).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 5.5.2 (txt l.1147-1149): Bukwen and Mashi added to Hamm's (2002) Beboid tree 'for which short wordlists are available (Koops and Blench 2008)'; 5.5.3 Phonology discusses only Mundabli vowels/pharyngealisation (Voll 2008). Bibliography: 'Koops, R. and R.M. Blench 2006. Bukwen and Mashi wordlists. ms.'

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2008. Beboid composite [comparative wordlists: Eastern Beboid (Nsari, Noone, Ncane, Mungong, Kemezung, Bebe, Cung) and Western Beboid (Abar, Missong, Bu, Mundabli, Koshin, Fang, Mbu', Mashi, Naki)]. ms., 9 pp., linked from Blench's 'Beboid page'.
sources.note: Nothing; wordlists only, and no Bukwen column at all (bukwen token count 0).

sources.citation: Hamm, Cameron. 2002. Beboid Language Family of Cameroon and Nigeria: Location and Genetic Classification. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002(-014?), 40 pp.
sources.note: Only other work whose Beboid tree includes Bukwen; a location/classification report, would at most confirm that no phonological data exist.
